transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-11-27
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 55 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Ravi Kapoor (Velox Head of ML), Elena Martinez (Velox Platform Eng), Sofia Chen (Velox PM), Tom Yu (Velox SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): quick runthrough of canary numbers, fallback plan, and who owns alerts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um today's the safety window rehearsal, so we want to lock thresholds and runbook steps. hope that's still good on your side.
[00:06] Ravi: yeah, thanks Jordan. we're good. we had one quick question before we start: how firm are the canary thresholds versus what we tested last week?
[00:12] Priya: right, so we iterated after the load test; last week's numbers were a bit optimistic. we've tightened the error-rate gate to 0.75% from 1.5% and latency p95 gate to 420ms for the short payload paths, long seqs we kept at 850ms. um those are the proposed numbers.
[00:28] Elena: and those latency numbers are for our dedicated config or hosted? we are in the dedicated pool right?
[00:33] Jordan: yes Velox is on a dedicated pool with reserved capacity, so these numbers reflect the dedicated profile with the quantized model. if you switch to hosted the p95 will be slightly different.
[00:42] Ravi: ok makes sense. Tom, from SRE perspective any concerns with the retention window? we need at least 30 days for the telemetry traces for audits.
[00:49] Tom: 30 days is fine. i just need to confirm how much the storage cost looks like if we enable detailed token-level breakdowns, last time that spiked a bit.
[00:56] Marco: we can show a cost delta chart; Redwood will include cost vs retention in the runbook.
[01:03] Sofia: can we, uh, just step through the traffic split plan — A/B or canary? i'm worried about product metrics noise.
[01:09] Priya: sure. recommendation is a staged canary with an initial 2% diverted traffic for 10 minutes, then 10% for 30 minutes, then 50% for an hour if gates pass, then full cutover. alternate is A/B where you split by user cohort, but that requires feature gating on your side.
[01:25] Ravi: we prefer cohort based A/B for feature comparisons, but for stability we want canary first. so plan: canary staged, then move to A/B for quality experiments.
[01:33] Jordan: excellent. during the canary we will run automated regression evals on your smoke prompts — that will run in parallel. if eval quality drops by more than 3% on BLEU-ish metric (or the fidelity score you already shared) we auto-fail.
[01:45] Elena: quick callout—what is the exact metric name again? last time the transcript had, uh, it said some different name.
[01:50] Priya: right it's the prompt fidelity score, we call it "Fidelity@1" in the evals sheet, but we can alias to product_fidelity in the dashboard.
[01:58] Tom: for monitoring, we want explicit Prometheus alerts. can we get the PromQL snippets now?
[02:02] Priya: yes i'll add them to the runbook. for example for p95 latency:
  - prometheus: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"redwood-runtime\"}[5m])) by (le))
  - error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"redwood-runtime\",code=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"redwood-runtime\"}[5m]))
there's some, um, fuzzy transcription of the metric names in the call but i'll put exact ones.
[02:32] Ravi: good. also we need to make sure KV cache warmup is accounted for in the first 5 minutes—the cold starts skewed last time.
[02:40] Priya: agreed. runbook will have a "priming" step: send a small prefix set to warm KV cache and mark that time window; the canary timer starts after the warmup period.
[02:50] Jordan: ok let's discuss rollback gates — what's the explicit failure criteria?
[02:54] Priya: gate triggers: error-rate > 0.75% sustained for 5 minutes, p95 latency > threshold for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows, fidelity drop > 3% on regression evals, or an SLO in your product metrics degrades (we'll link the specific Prometheus rules).
[03:11] Elena: and rolling back means automatic traffic cut to baseline model and alert page to SRE on-call, correct?
[03:16] Jordan: correct. Redwood's routing policy can immediately send traffic to the fallback model variant in the same pool. we'll also create a jittered fallback to avoid thundering herd.
[03:26] Tom: how fast is that fallback? what's the RTO?
[03:29] Priya: network routing change is sub-second, but full stabilization including cache warmup might take 30-90s depending on state. we'll recommend a 3-minute cool-down before re-evaluating.
[03:40] Ravi: ok. what about audit logs for the rollbacks? we need immutable logs for compliance.
[03:44] Marco: Redwood writes an audit event to the control plane and we can ship a copy to your SIEM via webhook or S3 archival. retention policy is configurable.
[03:53] Sofia: are we capturing per-token cost while canarying? product wants a cost delta in the runbook so finance can sign off.
[03:59] Jordan: yes token-level cost breakdown will be included; expectations shown as per-token and per-minute cost deltas between canary and baseline.
[04:06] Ravi: one more question — how do we handle partial failures, e.g., 10% of requests see higher latency because of a VM behind a single AZ, do we have region-aware routing?
[04:15] Priya: yes, routing supports region and AZ-aware policies. for the pilot you are single-region but we can route away from unhealthy AZs automatically based on health checks.
[04:25] Elena: timeline check — safety window proposed date?
[04:28] Jordan: we suggested 2025-12-03 during low product traffic between 02:00-04:00 your local timezone. does that still work?
[04:35] Sofia: yes that's fine. we'll coordinate calendars.
[04:38] Tom: can we do a dry-run on staging earlier, next Tuesday?
[04:41] Jordan: absolutely — agreed dry-run on staging 2025-12-01.
[04:45] Priya: let's go through the runbook steps now, high level: pre-window checklist, warmup, canary stage 1 (2% 10m), check gates, stage 2 (10% 30m), stage 3 (50% 60m), full cutover, post-cutover monitoring and rollback window.
[05:02] Sofia: for pre-window checklist who signs off? product and compliance?
[05:06] Marco: recommended: product lead (Sofia), Head of ML (Ravi), and your compliance or security lead. Redwood PM signs off on runbook completeness.
[05:15] Ravi: ok. can you also put a note about the SSO/SAML tokens we're using? compliance wants confirmation tokens aren't logged.
[05:21] Priya: yes tokens are masked in logs; only audit ids are stored. we'll include the redaction policy in the security appendix of the runbook.
[05:30] Elena: earlier you mentioned token-level breakdowns possibly increasing storage. can you provide an estimate?
[05:34] Jordan: yes we'll add a table: 30-day retention with token-level breakdown is approx +12% to telemetry storage cost for your volume, specific numbers in the runbook.
[05:42] Ravi: one minor doubt: our internal on-prem inference does not support the same quantization you use—does Redwood have a fallback model variant that is compatible for air-gapped customers?
[05:51] Priya: we do offer a private deployment package that can be deployed on-prem with a slightly different kernel set; for the pilot we are on dedicated hosted infra but we can map a fallback variant.
[05:59] Tom: ok good. let's capture the exact rollback steps in order so on-call knows what to press.
[06:05] Jordan: agreed. runbook will have a step-by-step checklist: 1) trigger rollback in console (button), 2) verify traffic has cut to fallback, 3) notify stakeholders, 4) run sanity check queries, 5) open a post-mortem if needed.
[06:18] Ravi: are there automatic diagnostic bundles created when rollback happens? that'd speed triage.
[06:22] Priya: yes we can auto-collect a diagnostic bundle (logs + KV cache snapshot + recent evals) and upload to your secure S3. note we redact PII by default.
[06:33] Sofia: quick note — product wants a control to pause A/B experiments automatically if baseline metrics change during canary. is that supported?
[06:40] Priya: yes you can set a linked guardrail so experiments pause if SLO drops. we'll show configuration in the dashboard.
[06:47] Elena: can we also attach a synthetic traffic generator to the runbook so we can reproduce issues deterministically?
[06:52] Jordan: Redwood provides a lightweight traffic generator you can run from staging; we'll include the script and sample payloads.
[06:59] Tom: about the PromQL snippets — could you also provide Grafana dashboard JSON export we can import?
[07:03] Priya: yes that's in scope. I'll attach dashboard json to the runbook artifact.
[07:08] Ravi: let's go over the thresholds quickly and confirm numbers: p95 short 420ms, p95 long 850ms, error-rate 0.75%, fidelity drop 3%, memory/GC alerts at 80% of instance mem.
[07:22] Priya: that's correct. Also add OOM rate check and swap usage check, we'll add container restarts >2 in 5m as a gate.
[07:32] Sofia: fine. will you document the exact playbooks for SRE? e.g., when a container restarts, is the step to roll back or to investigate?
[07:40] Marco: we typically recommend investigation for infra issues; automatic rollback for user-facing SLO degradations. we'll list decision matrix.
[07:49] Ravi: competitor question — we had a demo from Anthropic recently; they do model-level A/B but their rollback options are more manual. good to see Redwood is automated here.
[07:59] Jordan: yeah our focus is automated fallbacks and observable runbooks.
[08:03] Elena: any outstanding security docs we need? we saw SOC2 and the redaction policy but need encryption in transit/at rest specifics.
[08:10] Marco: we will share the security pack (SOC2, encryption at rest/TLS, KMS integration). expect that in an email after this call.
[08:18] Tom: one last thought: during the canary, if we see noisy signals due to user cohort differences, can we segment by header or cookie?
[08:24] Priya: yes session cookie or header-based routing is supported; we can annotate traffic so Grafana can filter.
[08:30] Sofia: ok, let's capture decision: follow staged canary, priming step, thresholds as listed, dry-run 2025-12-01 on staging, safety window 2025-12-03 for production, Redwood to deliver runbook updates and PromQL/grafana assets by 2025-11-29.
[08:44] Jordan: recording those next steps. any other blockers?
[08:47] Ravi: none from me.
[08:48] Elena: none.
[08:49] Tom: all good.
[08:50] Jordan: great thanks everyone. we'll share the updated runbook and the links to the dashboard. Marco will follow up with the security pack.
[08:58] Marco: thanks team, i'll add the meeting notes to the CRM and attach the action items.
[09:03] Sofia: thanks all. bye.
